newsitem.title: USA: GUARANTEE LIFE SEES MORE UNIT EXPENSE CUT.
newsitem.headline: GUARANTEE LIFE SEES MORE UNIT EXPENSE CUT.

text.p: Guarantee Life Cos said Thursday it expects an additional decrease in unit expense for the second half of 1997 and 1998.
The company, parent of Guarantee Life Insurance Co, made the forecast as it reported higher revenues and net operating income for the second quarter ended June 30.

Robert Bates, chairman and chief executive officer, also said the company's sales momentum achieved last year has been sustained during the first six months of 1997 in all three of its operating divisions.
Bates said the company was encouraged by ongoing expense reduction efforts and the increased operational efficiencies in its employee benefits infrastructure.
Operating expenses in the second quarter were 16.5 percent of total revenues compared to 17.7 percent for the first quarter of 1997 and 16.7 percent for the second quarter last year, he said.

For the second quarter of 1997, the company said it posted a net income from continuing operations, excluding realized investment gains, of $4.2 million, or $0.44 per share, compared to $4.3 million, or $0.43 per share, a year ago.

Revenues increased 17.5 percent to $85.4 million in the latest quarter, compared to $72.7 million for the same period in 1996. Net premiums and policyholder assessments were $61.3 million versus $50.1 million a year ago.

Net income from continuing operations for the first six months, excluding realized investment gains, increased 15.9 percent to $7.3 million, or $0.74 per share, from $6.3 million, or $0.64 per share during the same period in 1996.

For the first six months, revenues increased 14.5 percent to $164.9 million compared to $144.0 million in 1996. Net premiums and policyholder assessments were $117.3 million versus $100.4 million in the similar period a year ago. Thursday, 24 July 1997 11:19:19 ENDS nN24128081
